sentences.text: Platyognathus is an extinct reptile belonging to the class Reptilia and the superfamily Gobiosuchoidea within the broader group of crocodyliforms.
This small animal measured about 63 cm in total body length, with a skull approximately 5.6 cm long.

Its dentition featured four premaxillary teeth, up to twelve serrated maxillary teeth, and prominent caniniform teeth in the lower jaw that extended high enough to occlude outside a premaxilla-maxilla notch.
The body was protected by extensive osteoderms, including sculpted dorsal plates wider than they are long and flat ventral ones that may have armored the limbs.
The lower canine teeth possessed polygonal cross-sections caused by ridges and grooves, a unique structural adaptation.

Paired caniniform teeth, a feature not seen in other described crocodyliform taxa, have been recorded from an unidentified crocodyliform in the Lower Jurassic Kayenta Formation and a protosuchid in the Lower Jurassic McCoy Brook Formation in Nova Scotia.
Platyognathus was first named by Chung-Chien Young in 1944 based on a partial lower jaw discovered in 1939 from the Dark Red Beds of the Lower Lufeng Formation.
The holotype jaw consisted of 11 tooth sockets on the left side, 12 on the right side, and one broken caniniform tooth.
Unfortunately, the holotype specimen was either lost or destroyed during World War II.
In 1965, additional specimens from the Lower Lufeng Formation were referred to the genus Platyognathus.
A partial skull designated as a neotype for the genus was described in 1996, collected in 1984 from the Lower Lufeng formation in Yunnan.
This neotype skull revealed a distinctive curvature of the jugal bone that distinguishes Platyognathus from other protosuchians.
Due to a very small infratemporal fenestra and a mandibular symphysis extending to the seventh to ninth tooth, Platyognathus is considered more derived than Orthosuchus.
Fossils of Platyognathus have been found in the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian) Zhangjiawa Member of the Lower Lufeng Formation in Yunnan, China.
Platyognathus lived from the Sinemurian to the Tithonian stages, between 199.5 and 145.06 million years ago.
There is a debate regarding the classification of Platyognathus, with some studies suggesting it was a pseudosuchian related to Sphenosuchus and Pedeticosaurus, while most consider it a protosuchian.
Because the known material is incomplete, there is currently no adequate cladistic analysis to determine the exact phylogenetic position of Platyognathus within Protosuchia.
